OUR APPROACH

How a project starts.

Platform-agnostic advice means comparing vendors and tools against the work you need to do and the systems you already have.

  1. 01

    Describe what is happening

    You do not need a technical diagnosis. Start with what is getting in the way, who it affects and what you have already tried.

  2. 02

    Define the first piece of work

    Choose the systems or workflow to review. Confirm the documents, access arrangements, fee and schedule before work starts.

  3. 03

    Review the findings

    Discuss the findings and trade-offs, then decide which changes, documentation or training to prioritize.

COMMON QUESTIONS

Before you get in touch.

A few answers to help you choose where to start.

What if I do not know which service I need?

Start with a consultation. Describe the problem in your own words: where work gets held up, what is unreliable or which records are missing. You do not need to diagnose it or choose a technology first.

Can you help if our documentation is missing or outdated?

Yes. Documentation work can include organizing existing notes, updating network diagrams and creating missing system inventories or operating procedures. See the types of documentation available.

Can we assess an AI idea before buying tools?

Yes. AI analysis examines the task, data, systems and constraints before selecting an approach. It can include comparing models, hardware and architecture options. Read about an AI assessment.

Which areas do you serve?

IT/OT Express LLC is based in Holly Springs, North Carolina, and serves business owners in Wake County, the Triangle and throughout North Carolina.

Do we need to replace our existing tools?

A review starts with the systems you already have and the problem you want to solve. Advice covers different vendors and platforms. Replacing equipment or choosing new software is a decision to evaluate, not a prerequisite for the conversation.

What should I have ready for the first conversation?

A short description of the problem and the systems involved is enough to start. Existing notes, diagrams or examples of the work can help, but they do not need to be complete or organized.
